Spoke with Rob regarding the situation where an application was completed, marked as delivered, and used to obtain funding so parts could be ordered before the repairs were completed. He explained that this involved a specific customer who wanted to secure approval but keep the vehicle until the required parts arrived. Because he could not release the vehicle without ordering the parts, he marked the deal as delivered to receive funding.

I reminded Rob that this is not the correct process. The proper procedure is to obtain approval, complete all repairs on the vehicle, and only then mark the application as delivered once the work has been completed. Applications should not be marked as delivered at any point prior to the completion of repairs. Rob acknowledged the issue and stated that he will not do this again moving forward.

Full Comments:
Checked in via Maps Application 
Stopped by Noise Creations and had the opportunity to speak with Ralph regarding financing options and account setup.

During the visit, I provided Ralph with my business card and assisted him in getting fully set up on the new EasyPay Finance system. We also enrolled the location in a $20 Amazon spiff incentive program to encourage utilization and help drive financing activity.

Ralph shared that they are currently only using Synchrony for financing. He mentioned that Synchrony declines a significant number of customers, which creates missed sales opportunities. I explained that this is where EasyPay Finance can provide value by helping customers who may not qualify through traditional financing programs.

Full Comments:

For the month of May, the shop submitted 15 originated applications, but only 4 resulted in funded transactions. I noticed a high number of declined applications and asked for feedback to better understand the trend. Specifically, I wanted to confirm whether EasyPay was being presented first or only after customers had been declined by another financing provider.

Joey confirmed that the team is running EasyPay first, rather than using it as a secondary option after another lender declines the customer. I thanked him for the clarification and encouraged the team to continue offering EasyPay as their first financing option. I also let him know to reach out if they need any additional support or have questions moving forward.
